key_insight: Repeated evaluation reveals substantial LLM response variability in data visualisation and supervised learning, especially on medium and hard tasks.
engineering_relevance: Evaluate data science assistants across repeated runs to measure consistency alongside answer quality before deployment.
method: Introduce DS-QA: 100 university-level questions spanning 16 datasets and three difficulty levels.
Assess general response properties, coarse-grained quality metrics and task-specific metrics.
Evaluate OpenAI models using a Monte Carlo protocol with 100 repeated runs.
evidence_signal: Across DS-QA evaluations, responses varied substantially by task and difficulty; a 0.1 increase in word verbosity ratio corresponded to about 0.013 higher token verbosity ratio.
watch_item: Findings from OpenAI models and university-course questions may not generalise to other models or production workflows.
paper_title: One Run Is Not Enough: A Monte Carlo Protocol for Evaluating LLM Reliability on Data Science Tasks
